title: Bitonti–Dukes–Sagan conjecture on trivariate symmetries of vincular-pattern distributions
statement:
For $n\geq 1$, let $\mathfrak{S}_n$ be the set of permutations of $[n]$, and define

$$
P_n(p,q,r,s)=\sum_{\sigma\in\mathfrak{S}_n}p^{\mathrm{\underline{13}2}(\sigma)}q^{\mathrm{\underline{31}2}(\sigma)}r^{\mathrm{2\underline{13}}(\sigma)}s^{\mathrm{2\underline{31}}(\sigma)}.
$$

Here $\mathrm{\underline{13}2}(\sigma)$, $\mathrm{\underline{31}2}(\sigma)$, $\mathrm{2\underline{13}}(\sigma)$, and $\mathrm{2\underline{31}}(\sigma)$ denote the numbers of occurrences in $\sigma$ of the corresponding vincular patterns. **Bitonti–Dukes–Sagan's conjecture.** The following trivariate specializations of $P_n$ have the stated symmetries:

$$
P_n(1,q,r,s)=P_n(1,q,s,r),
$$

$$
P_n(p,1,r,s)=P_n(p,1,s,r),
$$

$$
P_n(p,q,1,s)=P_n(q,p,1,s),
$$

$$
P_n(p,q,r,1)=P_n(q,p,r,1).
$$

These identities assert additional symmetries beyond the known $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetries of the full four-variable polynomial $P_n$. They were supported empirically for $n\leq 11$ in the cited work; a proof or disproof of the trivariate symmetries remains open.
source_name: Joanna N. Chen, Shishuo Fu and Jiang Zeng, “An involution for trivariate symmetries of vincular patterns”, arXiv:2509.13097 (2025).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.13097

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2025).
